Sync explorer

How every synchronization graph was made, and the same process for any of the 996 trials. Pick a subject and trial below to see its recordings, motion signals, matching score and verdict.

How each graph is made

STEP 1

Load the five files

Each trial needs phone accelerometer, phone gyroscope, watch accelerometer, watch gyroscope and the Kinect skeleton. Readings are sorted by time; exact duplicate timestamps are dropped.

STEP 2

Turn readings into motion signals

  • Gyroscope → rotation speed √(x²+y²+z²), rad/s
  • Accelerometer → jolt |a − gravity|, m/s²; gravity = 1-second moving average
  • Skeleton → pelvis acceleration (from pelvis positions, m/s²) and torso rotation (how fast the pelvis-to-chest line turns, rad/s)

STEP 3

Slide and score

Resample to 30 readings per second. Slide the skeleton against the watch from −8 to +8 s in 1/30 s steps and score each position by correlation: 1 = same shape, 0 = unrelated.

STEP 4

Average per session

A real clock offset is the same in every trial of a session, so the score curves of all its trials are averaged. The peak is the session’s offset. A straight-line fit over the session absorbs slow drift of a few ms per minute.

STEP 5

Fine-tune and shift

Phone = reference, no shift. Watch: its session offset (always within ±0.06 s). Skeleton: this trial’s own peak if its score is at least 0.6 within ±0.5 s of the session value, otherwise the session value. The shift is added to every timestamp.

STEP 6

Keep and judge

Keep only the time all five files cover (at least 2 s). Flag holes over 1 s. For falls, the phone’s impact must sit inside the kept window. Copied files and missing files are discarded.

The raw data also holds two Meta sensors (wrist and hip). They served as a shared reference to measure each offset precisely; the direct skeleton-to-watch match shown here agrees within 0.15 s for 15 of 16 subjects. Accelerometer-only and gyroscope-only matching give the same session offsets within 0.13 s.
